questions.title: What a View Stores
questions.description: A regular (non-materialized) SQL view stores…
questions.Option1: A full copy of the rows taken at creation time
questions.Option2: The SELECT query itself — rows are computed when the view is queried
questions.Option3: Only the primary keys of the underlying rows
questions.Option4: An index over the base table

questions.title: Create a View Statement
questions.description: Which statement correctly creates a view named v_active over all columns of bookings?
questions.Option2: MAKE VIEW v_active AS SELECT * FROM bookings;
questions.Option3: CREATE VIEW v_active INSERT SELECT * FROM bookings;
questions.Option4: CREATE VIEW v_active AS SELECT * FROM bookings;

questions.title: Views Track Base Data
questions.description: v_room_rates was created over rooms (8 rows). What does the snippet print?
questions.Option1: 8 — views snapshot their rows at creation time
questions.Option2: 9 — the view sees the newly inserted row
questions.Option4: An error — INSERT against a viewed table is illegal

questions.title: Dropping a View
questions.description: Which statement removes the view v_tmp?

questions.title: Simple Updatable View
questions.description: Which kind of view is updatable in SQLite (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE allowed through it)?
questions.Option3: A simple single-table view with no aggregates or DISTINCT

questions.title: Materialized Views in SQLite
questions.description: Does SQLite support materialized views?
questions.Option4: No — SQLite provides regular views only

questions.title: View vs Table
questions.description: Pick the accurate contrast between a table and a regular view.
questions.Option1: Views hold data; tables hold queries
questions.Option2: Tables hold data; views are saved queries computed over tables
questions.Option3: Views are always faster than tables
questions.Option4: Tables cannot be indexed once views exist

questions.title: Filter Through the View
questions.description: rooms holds two deluxe rooms: 201 at 180.0 and 202 at 175.0. What does the snippet return?
questions.Option1: 2 — the outer WHERE is ignored for views
questions.Option2: 0 — WHERE cannot be combined with a view
questions.Option3: 1 — the outer WHERE filters the rows the view yields
questions.Option4: An error — views cannot be filtered

questions.title: Aggregates Inside Views
questions.description: Can a view definition contain GROUP BY and aggregate functions in SQLite?
questions.Option1: Yes — a view may aggregate its base tables
questions.Option2: No — views may only project plain columns
questions.Option4: Only one aggregate per view is allowed

questions.title: Nested Views
questions.description: May a view be defined on top of another view?
questions.Option3: Allowed only when the base is materialized
questions.Option4: Allowed — views can reference other views

questions.title: List the Views
questions.description: What does the final SELECT in this snippet return?
questions.Option2: v_a and v_b — one row per view
questions.Option3: Only v_a — the first one created

questions.title: Updatability Breakers
questions.description: Adding which element to a single-table view definition typically makes the view non-updatable?

questions.title: Refreshing Materialized Views
questions.description: For databases that support materialized views, what does refreshing one mean?
questions.Option1: Recomputing the stored rows from the base tables
questions.Option2: Deleting and recreating the view definition text
questions.Option3: Rebuilding the indexes on the view
questions.Option4: Re-running CREATE VIEW with a new name

questions.title: Duplicate View Name
questions.description: What happens when this script runs?
questions.Option1: The second definition silently replaces the first
questions.Option2: An error — a view named v_x already exists
questions.Option3: Both are kept, the second renamed v_x_1
questions.Option4: The second becomes a real table
questions.codesnippet:
CREATE VIEW v_x AS SELECT 1 AS a;
CREATE VIEW v_x AS SELECT 2 AS b;

questions.title: IF NOT EXISTS Views
questions.description: v_x already exists. What does CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS v_x AS SELECT 1; do in SQLite?
questions.Option1: Replaces the old view with the new definition
questions.Option4: Skips creation and keeps the existing view

questions.title: Why Serve Views
questions.description: Best reason an operations team exposes views instead of base tables to applications?
questions.Option1: Restrict visible columns and rows and shield schema changes behind a stable interface
questions.Option2: Views are always faster than base tables
questions.Option3: Views store an extra copy that serves as backup
questions.Option4: Views disable locking on the base tables

questions.title: View on a View
questions.description: rooms rates are 120, 115.5, 130, 180, 175, 260, 240 and 420. What does the snippet print?
questions.Option1: 5 — the chained filters collapse into one
questions.Option4: An error — chained views are invalid
